correctness.rationale: A universal proof reduces every length g+2 odd closed walk at girth>=g to either a simple length-(g+2) cycle or a length-g cycle with one reversal. Square-freeness freezes injective walks and makes cells single-coordinate simplices. Off-core simplices attach on cycle edges and collapse relatively. The remaining Hom(C_(g+2),C_g) is two polygons of g(g+2) vertices. Eight finite target graph instances independently verify component counts and signed Euler dimensions; finite checks are supporting evidence, not proof.

Fujii–Kimura–Nozaki provides an algorithmic general result, but its manuscript was inaccessible, creating a material unresolved duplication risk; an explicit formula with its own direct proof remains a distinct claim based on accessible material, not a claim of proved uniqueness.

value.rationale: A first-beyond-girth threshold gives a complete, infinite high-girth graph-family topological classification in terms of two intrinsic simple-cycle counts. It distinguishes nonhomotopic source mapping components and recovers the numbers of shortest odd cycles and next odd cycles simultaneously; it covers irregular and branching target graphs including the Petersen graph, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The known squarefree point-or-circle theorem alone cannot furnish this census.
